title: Cap. VIII: VI Ex vs.19 — same imputation? Deny the minor
pass_a_gloss: Head VI begins. Placeus asks whether the contested thesis finally appears from Romans 5:19, quoting the parallel: through one person's disobedience many were made sinners, and through one person's obedience many will be made righteous. Answer first: no, not at all. Opponent D. Garissoles (D. G.) builds more than one proof from the verse. Proof one runs: in this verse Paul is still doing the work he developed at greater length in the preceding verses; and here he obviously discusses imputation; so those preceding verses must also concern that same imputation. Placeus targets the middle claim (the minor). Either Paul is not discussing imputation in this verse at all, or, if imputation is in view, it is not the immediate / prior-to-corruption kind — and that is the only kind Placeus refuses. Chain: if verse 19 merely continues the earlier verses, and those earlier verses already showed Paul was not teaching that refused kind of imputation, then verse 19 does not teach it either.
pass_b_english: VI. But perhaps that thesis will finally surface from verse 19: "As through one man's disobedience many were constituted sinners, so through one man's obedience many will be constituted righteous" (Romans 5:19). In no way. D. Garissoles argues from it in more than one form, and first thus: the Apostle in this verse is doing what he had pursued more diffusely in those earlier ones; but in this verse he plainly treats imputation; therefore the earlier verses must be understood of the same imputation. I answer the minor: in this verse the Apostle is not treating imputation; or if he is, he is not treating immediate or antecedent imputation — the only kind I deny. For if he is doing in this verse what he did in the earlier ones, where it was plain he was not treating that imputation, it follows that he is not treating that imputation in this verse either.
source_text: VI. Sed fortasse illa tandem aliquando emerget ex verf. 19. Sicut per unius inobedientiam peccatores constituti sunt multi, ita per unius obedientiam justi constituentur multi: Nullo certe modo. Argumentatur ex eo D. G. non uno modo, & primo quidem sic. Idem Apostolus agit hoc versu quod reliquis illis diffusiùs prosecutus fuerat. Atqui hoc versu manifeste agit de imputatione. Ergo & de eadem imputatione superiora intelligenda sunt. Respondeo ad minorem, Apostolum hoc versu non agere de imputatione: aut si agit de imputatione, non agere de imputatione immediata seu antecedente, quam solam nego. Nam si idem agit hoc versu quod in superioribus, in quibus de ista imputatione eum non egisse patuit, consequens est, eum de ista imputatione non agere in isto versu.
